title: Agentic Trading: When LLM Agents Meet Financial Markets
authors: Yihan Xia; Panpan You; Taotao Wang; Fang Liu; Han Qi; Xiaoxiao Wu; Shengli Zhang
key_contribution: Reviews 77 LLM trading-agent studies and highlights protocol incomparability, weak transaction-cost reporting, and poor reproducibility.
main_limitation: Survey lens rather than a validated final taxonomy; field still immature.
relevance_to_project_aegis: Core evidence for reproducibility and evaluation gap

title: TradingAgents: Multi-Agents LLM Financial Trading Framework
authors: Yijia Xiao; Edward Sun; Di Luo; Wei Wang
key_contribution: Models a trading firm with role-specialized agents such as fundamental analyst sentiment analyst technical analyst trader bull/bear researchers and risk managers.
main_limitation: Performance claims require strict reproducibility and transaction-cost review.

title: FinMem: A Performance-Enhanced LLM Trading Agent with Layered Memory and Character Design
authors: Yangyang Yu; Haohang Li; Zhi Chen; Yuechen Jiang; Yang Li; Denghui Zhang; Rong Liu; Jordan W. Suchow; Khaldoun Khashanah
key_contribution: Introduces profiling, layered memory, and decision-making modules for financial trading agents.
main_limitation: Memory is trading-decision focused; broader thesis and macro memory remain underdeveloped.

title: Finance Agent Benchmark: Benchmarking LLMs on Real-world Financial Research Tasks
authors: Antoine Bigeard; Langston Nashold; Rayan Krishnan; Shirley Wu
key_contribution: Builds a benchmark of 537 expert-authored finance research questions using SEC filings and an agentic tool harness with Google Search and EDGAR access.
main_limitation: Best model accuracy reported as below 50 percent, showing current limitations; benchmark is still mainly task-answering rather than full portfolio workflow.
relevance_to_project_aegis: Core evidence for real-world finance research task difficulty

title: Evaluation and Benchmarking Suite for Financial Large Language Models and Agents
authors: Shengyuan Lin; Kaiwen He; Jaisal Patel; Qinchuan Zhang; Chris Ding; James Tang; Keyi Wang; Yupeng Cao; Yan Wang; Kairong Xiao; Vincent Caldeira; Matt White; Xiao-Yang Liu Yanglet
key_contribution: Presents a suite covering the lifecycle of FinLLMs and FinAgents, including evaluation pipeline, governance framework, leaderboard, AgentOps framework, and documentation platform.
main_limitation: Very broad suite; investment-research-specific audit and thesis workflow still need refinement.
relevance_to_project_aegis: Important for evaluation lifecycle and governance framing

title: FinRobot: AI Agent for Equity Research and Valuation with Large Language Models
authors: Tianyu Zhou; Pinqiao Wang; Yilin Wu; Hongyang Yang
key_contribution: Designs an equity research agent with Data-CoT, Concept-CoT, and Thesis-CoT agents for company analysis, valuation, risk assessment, and research report generation.
main_limitation: Needs stronger independent evaluation against professional analyst workflows and audit standards.
relevance_to_project_aegis: Highly relevant to shift from trading agents to investment research agents

title: When AI Meets Finance (StockAgent): Large Language Model-based Stock Trading in Simulated Real-world Environments
authors: Chong Zhang; Xinyi Liu; Zhongmou Zhang; Mingyu Jin; Lingyao Li; Zhenting Wang; Wenyue Hua; Dong Shu; Suiyuan Zhu; Xiaobo Jin; Sujian Li; Mengnan Du; Yongfeng Zhang
key_contribution: Develops StockAgent, an LLM-based multi-agent system to simulate investor trading behavior in realistic market environments and avoid test-set leakage.
main_limitation: Primarily trading simulation rather than investment research; reproduction and cost assumptions require full-text extraction.

title: Evaluating Financial Intelligence in Large Language Models: Benchmarking SuperInvesting AI with LLM Engines
authors: Akshay Gulati; Kanha Singhania; Tushar Banga; Parth Arora; Anshul Verma; Vaibhav Kumar Singh; Agyapal Digra; Jayant Singh Bisht; Danish Sharma; Varun Singla; Shubh Garg
key_contribution: Introduces AFIB, a multi-dimensional financial intelligence benchmark across factual accuracy, completeness, data recency, consistency, and failure patterns.
main_limitation: Benchmark appears system-comparison oriented and may not be agent-specific; requires verification.

title: StockBench: Can LLM Agents Trade Stocks Profitably In Real-world Markets?
authors: Yanxu Chen; Zijun Yao; Yantao Liu; Jin Ye; Jianing Yu; Lei Hou; Juanzi Li
key_contribution: Introduces a contamination-free benchmark for LLM agents in realistic multi-month stock trading environments with return, drawdown, and Sortino metrics.
main_limitation: Trading benchmark rather than investment research workflow; requires cost and reproducibility extraction.
relevance_to_project_aegis: Useful benchmark for dynamic trading-agent evaluation

title: FinRpt: Dataset Evaluation System and LLM-based Multi-agent Framework for Equity Research Report Generation
authors: Song Jin; Shuqi Li; Shukun Zhang; Rui Yan
key_contribution: Frames equity research report generation as a task, introduces dataset construction pipeline, 11-metric evaluation system, and multi-agent framework FinRpt-Gen.
main_limitation: Requires full extraction of dataset construction, metrics, and evaluation before use as core evidence.
relevance_to_project_aegis: High-priority candidate for investment research agent category

title: TrustTrade: Human-Inspired Selective Consensus Reduces Decision Uncertainty in LLM Trading Agents
authors: Minghan Li; Rachel Gonsalves; Weiyue Li; Sunghoon Yoon; Mengyu Wang
key_contribution: Introduces selective consensus to reduce uniform-trust bias, misinformation amplification, hallucination volatility, and unstable risk-return behavior in LLM trading agents.
main_limitation: Trading-agent focus; claims require full-text extraction and independent evaluation.

title: TradingGPT: Multi-Agent System with Layered Memory and Distinct Characters for Enhanced Financial Trading Performance
authors: Yang Li; Yangyang Yu; Haohang Li; Zhi Chen; Khaldoun Khashanah
key_contribution: Introduces layered memory and distinct agent characters for financial trading, related to FinMem lineage.
main_limitation: Trading-focused and likely overlaps conceptually with FinMem; requires relation check.
